summary:
The HEARTS Act of 2024 (Public Law 118-176) amends the Public Health Service Act to authorize and support cardiomyopathy education, awareness, risk assessment, research, and AED training in schools. The operative mechanism inserts four new sections (312A through 312D) after section 312 of the PHSA (42 U.S.C. 244).

Section 312A (42 U.S.C. 244a) directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services, in consultation with the CDC Director, to develop public education materials and resources on high-risk cardiac conditions, AED placement guidelines, and cardiac emergency response plans within 18 months of enactment. The Secretary must disseminate these materials within 30 months of enactment through state educational agencies, state and local health departments, and the CDC public website. The section establishes definitions for terms including "cardiomyopathy" and incorporates definitions from section 8101 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965.

Section 312B (42 U.S.C. 244b) requires the Secretary, acting through the CDC Director, to submit a report to Congress within 18 months of enactment on existing CDC activities regarding the prevalence and epidemiology of cardiomyopathy, subject to applicable federal and state privacy laws. It further requires the Secretary to develop and make publicly available a cardiomyopathy risk assessment, mandating the CDC Director to seek input from external stakeholders, including patient advocacy organizations and medical professional societies.

Section 312C (42 U.S.C. 244c) authorizes the Secretary, in consultation with the NIH Director, to expand and coordinate NIH research activities on cardiomyopathy, subject to a nonduplication requirement. It mandates a report to Congress within 18 months of enactment outlining ongoing NIH research and identifying future research agendas for adult and pediatric populations.

Section 312D (42 U.S.C. 244d) authorizes the Secretary to award grants to local educational agencies (LEAs), in consultation with qualified health care entities, to develop and implement AED and CPR programs in public elementary and secondary schools. Grant funds may be used for materials, training, cardiac emergency response plans, and purchasing AEDs approved, cleared, or classified under sections 515, 510(k), or 513(f)(2) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, along with necessary maintenance. 

Section 2(b) specifies that no additional funds are authorized to be appropriated to carry out the newly inserted sections 312A through 312D, establishing an authorization of activities without a corresponding new appropriation.
